requirements.requirement: Record every command run through sudo on node1, with user and timestamp, to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers.d snippet (Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year, log_host) was installed with correct permissions and validated with visudo -cf/-c. Test sudo commands (true, id -u, echo, wc, journalctl, cat) all appeared in the dedicated log with full timestamp (including year), host, user, PWD, and COMMAND fields, directly demonstrating the requirement.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log (syslog/secure/messages/journald)
requirements.summary: Defaults !syslog was added to suppress the authpriv syslog entries. Marker strings generated via sudo were confirmed present only in /var/log/sudo-commands.log and explicitly absent from /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journalctl output, both before and after the reboot.

overall_summary: Both material requirements of the task — logging every sudo command with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and keeping those entries out of the general system log — are directly satisfied with concrete before/after evidence (marker-string tests present in the dedicated log and absent from secure/messages/journald, both pre- and post-reboot). The sudoers.d configuration was syntax-validated at each step. The independently required node-restart protocol was also executed well, showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, a bounded unreachability window, a changed boot identity, and fully recovered/functional sudo logging afterward. The only blemish is a small unneeded /tmp/mark_epoch file left behind from an intermediate step.
limitations: Restart evidence (boot identity change, service recovery) pertains to the provider-wide protocol rather than the task contract itself, which does not require reboot persistence; it is reported for completeness and did not affect material task outcome scoring.

No evidence was captured of a non-root user invoking sudo (only root-invoked test commands were shown), though the sudoers Defaults directive applies globally regardless of invoking user, so this does not weaken confidence in the configuration's correctness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all executor commands were read-only discovery/verification or directly necessary for the task (writing the sudoers snippet, pre-creating the log file with tight 0600 permissions, validating syntax). The reboot (cmd-f8a502b6156c4a96) and subsequent polling (cmd-ec3db24350cb4a26, cmd-22bf41edb27241af, cmd-7fecef7cf4df4cf6, cmd-4dab2e79b5f24443) constitute the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol, not a task requirement, but were executed cleanly with a documented pre-restart healthy baseline, acknowledged reboot, bounded unreachability window, and confirmed new boot identity plus recovered sudo-logging service state (cmd-8c62a6837667472c, cmd-f8a502b6156c4a96, cmd-4dab2e79b5f24443, cmd-634b288fac7449db) — solid restart evidence even though not contractually required. One minor unnecessary residue: step 6 of cmd-2181a3f4158c4b7a ran `date +%s > /tmp/mark_epoch`, writing a throwaway file with no documented purpose in the final solution; it was never cleaned up and is visible as an added file in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. Low-risk, non-destructive, but left in place unnecessarily.
